Legal Standards.name: Delta Reform Act
Legal Standards.note: Establishes overarching state policy and governance framework for the Sacramento–San Joaquin Delta, including coordination of water supply reliability and ecosystem protection.

Legal Standards.name: Bay-Delta Water Quality Control Plan (Bay-Delta Plan)
Legal Standards.note: Defines water quality objectives and beneficial uses for the Bay-Delta; serves as a foundational document in the legal hierarchy governing Delta exports.

Legal Standards.name: Porter-Cologne Water Quality Control Act
Legal Standards.note: California’s primary water quality law providing authority for state regulation of surface and groundwater quality, including implementation of Bay-Delta standards.

Legal Standards.name: California Water Code
Legal Standards.note: Statutory framework governing water rights, allocation, and administration in California, operating alongside Porter-Cologne and Delta-specific mandates.

Legal Standards.name: Federal Clean Water Act (CWA)
Legal Standards.note: Provides the federal legal basis for water quality standards; Bay-Delta objectives are treated as CWA water quality standards with EPA oversight.

Legal Standards.name: Endangered Species Act (ESA)
Legal Standards.note: Imposes additional federal constraints on Delta operations to protect listed species, influencing export and flow requirements.

Legal Standards.name: Delta Stewardship Council Agricultural Salinity Standards
Legal Standards.note: State mandate for agricultural beneficial uses in the Delta, developed by the Delta Stewardship Council using best available science; applies to USBR/CVP operations only.

key_elements.note: Additional salinity standards exist for municipal and industrial (M&I) uses.

Tier 1.policy_name: SWRCB Water Quality Control Plan Decision D-1641
Tier 1.note: D-1641 salinity objectives are used by water managers as measurements approach legal thresholds.
Reservoir releases may be used to dilute salinity, but are often driven by other mandates such as water temperature or environmental requirements.
Curtailments may be used to address salinity but are legally triggered by lack of water supply (e.g., drought conditions), not salinity alone.
Curtailments based on special permit terms for junior rights holders, typically tied to upstream storage and water availability rather than salinity thresholds.
Other policy responses such as salinity barriers are generally not activated at this tier.
If a drought emergency is declared, SWP/DWR and CVP/USBR may file Temporary Urgency Change Petitions/Orders (TUCP/O) to modify water rights, which implicates D-1641.

Tier 2.policy_name: Observed salinity exceedances under current climate conditions
Tier 2.note: These salinity levels occur sporadically during very dry or extremely dry years.
Salinity levels at this tier are consistent with likely seawater intrusion in the Delta.
Drought emergency declaration becomes likely under these conditions.
Water Code and SWRCB authority allow temporary relaxation of D-1641 salinity standards via TUCP/O during drought emergencies.

Tier 3.note: Thresholds are currently rare in California water management but may occur under an unknown future climate regime.
Governor-declared extreme drought emergency is expected at this tier.
Structural salinity barriers would almost certainly be deployed to prevent further seawater intrusion.

Tier 3.policy_name: TUCP/O salinity standards relaxation (very extreme drought)
Tier 3.note: Temporary relaxation of salinity standards would likely be approved for very extreme drought conditions.

Tier 4.note: Represents an almost unknown water future requiring extreme measures for human survival, as described in emergency water planning literature.
California regions are encouraged to maintain sufficient water storage to last several water years.
Salinity standards would likely be relaxed for multiple consecutive years under emergency authority.

Tier 4.policy_name: State and federal water project operations
Tier 4.note: CVP/SWP operations would likely be limited to food-security-level agriculture and basic human needs under state emergency planning.
Curtailments and salinity barriers initiated in earlier stages would likely remain in place.
